# Known vulnerable PRODUCTION dependencies of apps/web, as locked on 2026-09-30.
# Only high and critical are listed: that is all the gate counts (--min-severity high).
# Regenerate: (cd apps/web && pnpm audit --prod --json > r.json); then
#   python3 apps/api/scripts/ci/audit_gate.py --kind pnpm --report r.json --baseline /dev/null --print-baseline
#
# Every line below is an EXPOSURE THE PRODUCT CARRIES TODAY, written down so the audit gate
# can tell a newly published advisory (or a newly pinned vulnerable version) from a standing
# one. It is NOT a judgement that the advisory is harmless, and nothing here is "accepted risk"
# in the sense of somebody having decided to live with it: the upgrades are engineering-03's.
#
# THIS FILE MAY ONLY SHRINK. When a dependency is upgraded, delete its lines; the gate prints
# which lines have gone stale. Adding a line is a decision and belongs in a review with the
# reason written beside it. apps/api/scripts/ci/audit_gate.py is the reader and explains why
# the gate is a ratchet instead of "fail on anything".
#
# Format: one advisory id per line, then `# package version [severity] - title (fix: ...)`.

GHSA-3PQ3-5FJ3-CG6V      # axios 1.16.1 [high] — Axios: HTTP/2 adapter bypasses configured DNS lookup and proxy controls (fix: >=1.20.0)

GHSA-GCFJ-64VW-6MP9      # axios 1.16.1 [high] — Axios Node HTTP adapter can use an inherited proxy after interceptor config cloning (fix: >=1.18.0)
# Added 30-09-2026: the baseline did not name this advisory, so running the gate over this branch reported it NEW
# and the dependency-audit job would have failed on the pull request that introduced it.
# Same package, same version and the same fix (axios >=1.20.0) as the six axios lines around it, so it is carried
# for the same reason: engineering-03's upgrade clears all seven together. Nothing in apps/web imports axios
# (it is declared in package.json and used by no source file), so that upgrade, or removing the dependency, is
# the cheapest one on this list.
